Plan C: Bitcoin Power Law Isn’t Broken, but Popular Models Overstated Its Fair Value
> His model places fair value near $98,517 vs. the $146,725 estimate of standard models.
> He believes BTC now sits near its lowest level relative to its long-term trend, a level reached on only about 60 days in its history.
Source:
https://x.com/TheRealPlanC/status/2125441027989291260

tweet.text:
Is the Bitcoin Power Law Broken? 

Math > Emotions. 

The following is NOT Financial Advice. 

My long-term conviction has not changed, but I'm surprised by how many people are having serious doubts right now. 

My simple theory: inaccurate models led to inflated expectations. 

I'll go into why in a second, but first: based on my model, Bitcoin is currently at the 1st percentile. 

Of its 5,974 daily closes, only about 60 have been below that line, roughly two months of its entire history.

Below that, my model's 0.1 percentile currently sits at $55,185, and Bitcoin has closed under it on only 6 days.

What does this all mean? 

Through a math-based lens, today's close puts Bitcoin at a historically low point relative to its long-term trend, one we have only seen on about 60 days since its inception.

Now, back to those inaccurate models. 

I have been saying for years that the vanilla OLS power law model in calendar time (price vs time) has serious issues. It has overstated the trend
